newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy March PPI, WPI growth seen subdued.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy March PPI, WPI growth seen subdued.

text.p: Italian wholesale and producer prices due this week are expected to show price pressures remained subdued in March, according to a Reuter survey of 12 economists.

March PPI data due on Tuesday is expected to show prices growing at 0.1 percent on a month-on-month basis and 0.8 percent year-on-year, compared with February's flat monthly rate and year-on-year growth of 0.8 percent.

Paolo Casadio, analyst at Credito Italiano, whose PPI forecasts were in line with the average of the analysts' estimates, said: "Certainly the increase in food prices in dollar terms will have an effect but will be toned down by the fall in energy prices and other prime materials."

Analysts on average forecast March wholesale prices unchanged on February and growing 0.5 percent year on year. This would compare with a fall in February of 0.1 percent and a gain on an annual basis of 0.5 percent.

Gianluca Sanna at Stone & McCarthy noted fuel prices had fallen in February and March and this should affect prices of intermediate goods which count for 55.5 percent on the overall index, leaving them unchanged on the month.
Lucia Trevisan at Caboto, who saw PPI up 0.1 percent month on month, said this was not a significant rise but merely a correction after a series of flat and falling rates recently.
Italian statistics institute Istat will release both WPI and PPI on Tuesday.
